definition_zh: v. 啁啾，吱吱叫；n. （鸟或昆虫的）啁啾声，短促的哔声
definition_en: to make the short high sound of a small bird or insect; such a sound
core_image: 窗台上麻雀一下一下地叫
scene: 天刚亮，麻雀就在窗台上叫个不停。Sparrows chirped on the sill at first light.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chirp 指鸟的啁啾声；句意是天刚亮麻雀就在窗台上叫个不停。

senses.title: The sound of a small bird
senses.definition: a short high note made by a small bird or insect
senses.definitionCN: 小鸟或昆虫发出的短促高音
senses.example: A single chirp came from the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 树篱里传来一声啁啾。
senses.why: The word is probably imitative of the sound itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能是对声音本身的模仿。

senses.title: A short electronic beep
senses.definition: a brief high signal from a machine, such as a smoke alarm
senses.definitionCN: 烟雾报警器等装置发出的短促高音
senses.example: The alarm chirps when the battery is low.
senses.exampleCN: 电池电量低时报警器会短促鸣叫。
senses.why: The bird sound was borrowed for small machines.
senses.whyCN: 鸟鸣声被借来形容小型装置的声音。

intro.en: Chirp is an imitative word, formed to sound like the note it names.
intro.cn: chirp 是拟声词，读音就在模仿它所命名的声音。

items.en: The word copies a short high bird note.
items.cn: 这个词模仿鸟的短促高音。

items.en: Chirp appears in English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪出现在英语中。

items.en: Nature writers use chirp for insects too.
items.cn: 十九世纪博物写作也用它指昆虫。

items.en: Small machines are said to chirp.
items.cn: 二十世纪小型装置也被形容为 chirp。

items.en: The noun and the verb are equally common.
items.cn: 现代名词与动词同样常用。

note.en: The look-alike group circles the chirp sound; the near-meaning group names other bird notes.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 chirp 的读音；近义组列出其他鸟鸣说法。

entries.definition: A series of light bird sounds.

normalIntro.en: The word is the sound: chirp, chirp, from the sill.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是那个声音：啾、啾，从窗台传来。

normal.en: Say chirp quickly.
It sounds like a small bird.
Sparrows chirp at dawn.
Crickets chirp at night.
A smoke alarm also chirps.
normal.cn: 烟雾报警器也会短促鸣叫。

abstract.en: A sound with feathers.
Morning arriving one note at a time.
A machine imitating a bird.

examples.en: A sparrow chirped once and flew off.
examples.cn: 一只麻雀叫了一声就飞走了。

examples.en: The chirp of crickets filled the garden.
examples.cn: 蟋蟀的鸣声充满花园。

examples.en: The detector chirps until you change the battery.
examples.cn: 探测器会一直短鸣，直到你换电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啾扑」——小鸟啾啾，扑棱翅膀。

root: 拟声词（模仿鸟叫）→ 英语 chirp

sensesIntro.en: One imitative word covers birds at dawn and alarms at night.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个拟声词既写黎明的小鸟，也写夜里的报警器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small beak opening on a windowsill
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上张开的小喙

branches.en: A sparrow on a cold sill.
branches.cn: 冷窗台上的一只麻雀。

branches.en: Crickets under a garden stone.
branches.cn: 花园石下的蟋蟀。

branches.en: A detector blinking on a ceiling.
branches.cn: 天花板上闪光的探测器。

branches.en: A low battery warning at night.
branches.cn: 夜里电量不足的提示。

branches.en: A tiny high note, alive or electric.
branches.cn: 一声细小高音，或活物或电流。

intro.en: Chirp is imitative; the list below adds words of small sounds and birds.
intro.cn: chirp 是拟声词；下面列出细小声音与鸟类词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin avis is a bird and sonus is sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为鸟，sonus 意为声音。

latinEntries.exampleCN: avis 产生 avian 与 aviary。
sonus 产生 sound 与 sonic。
cantare 产生 chant 与 canticle。

definition_zh: 叶绿素；植物与藻类中捕获光能的绿色色素
definition_en: the green pigment in plants and algae that captures light for photosynthesis
core_image: 一层绿色染料铺在叶肉里，专门把红光和蓝紫光收进来
scene: 湖水的取样瓶过滤后颜色偏绿，绿色越深，说明水里的藻类越多。Chlorophyll readings tell how much algae is in the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 chlorophyll 是「叶绿素含量」（第 3 个义项：作为可以测定的浓度指标）；句意：叶绿素的测定值能说明湖里藻类有多少。

pos.zh: 叶绿素（不可数，指这种色素）
叶绿素分子；某一类叶绿素（可数）

derivatives.zh: 叶绿素衍生物（食品色素）

senses.title: The green pigment
senses.titleCN: 绿色素：把光收进来的染料
senses.definition: the green pigment found in plants and algae that absorbs light
senses.definitionCN: 植物与藻类中的绿色色素，负责吸收光
senses.example: Chlorophyll gives the leaf its colour.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素赋予叶片颜色。
senses.why: The word names a substance before it names anything else: a pigment, green, and sitting in the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先命名一种物质：一种绿色的、待在叶子里的色素。

senses.title: A molecular type
senses.titleCN: 分子类型：甲、乙等不同结构
senses.definition: one of several closely related pigment molecules, distinguished by small structural differences
senses.definitionCN: 几种结构相近的叶绿素分子之一（如甲、乙两种）
senses.example: The two main chlorophylls absorb slightly different wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 两种主要的叶绿素吸收的波长略有不同。
senses.why: Chemistry counts the variants, so the mass noun also has a plural for the distinct molecules.
senses.whyCN: 化学要数这些变体，于是这个不可数名词也有了指不同分子的复数。

senses.title: Measured content
senses.titleCN: 含量：单位面积或体积里有多少
senses.definition: the amount of the pigment present, measured as a concentration
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素含量：以浓度计的量
senses.example: Chlorophyll readings tell how much algae is in the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素的测定值能说明湖里藻类有多少。
senses.why: Once the pigment can be extracted and read, the word shifts from the substance to the number.
senses.whyCN: 色素一旦能被提取和读数，这个词就从物质转到了那个数。

senses.title: Fluorescence signal
senses.titleCN: 荧光：受光后发出的微弱红光
senses.definition: the faint red glow the pigment emits when excited, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素受激后发出的微弱红光，用作检测信号
senses.example: Chlorophyll fluorescence shows how hard the leaf is working.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素荧光显示叶片有多用力。
senses.why: The pigment absorbs light and can re-emit a little of it; instruments read that re-emission as a stress signal.
senses.whyCN: 色素吸收光，也能重新发出一点光；仪器把这点重新发出的光读成胁迫信号。

senses.title: Absorption bands
senses.titleCN: 吸收带：偏爱红光与蓝紫光
senses.definition: the particular wavelengths the pigment absorbs, mainly red and blue-violet
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素主要吸收红光与蓝紫光的波段
senses.example: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素吸收红光与蓝光，反射绿光。
senses.why: The colour we see is the light the pigment refuses; what it takes is the red and the blue-violet.
senses.whyCN: 我们看到的颜色是色素不要的光；它拿走的是红光与蓝紫光。

senses.title: Food colour
senses.titleCN: 食品色素：作为着色剂使用
senses.definition: the pigment used as a colouring agent in food or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 作为食品或药品着色剂的叶绿素
senses.example: Chlorophyll is listed as a green food colour.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素被列为一种绿色食品着色剂。
senses.why: Because it is green and edible, industry uses the substance as a dye rather than as a light catcher.
senses.whyCN: 因为它绿且可食，工业把它当染料用，而不是当捕光器。

senses.title: Derivative salts
senses.titleCN: 衍生物：铜钠盐等稳定形式
senses.definition: a stabilised derivative of the pigment, such as a copper salt, used commercially
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素的稳定衍生物，如铜钠盐
senses.example: The label lists chlorophyllin rather than chlorophyll.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上写的是叶绿素衍生物，而不是叶绿素。
senses.why: The natural pigment fades, so industry modifies it; the derivative keeps the green and loses the light work.
senses.whyCN: 天然色素会褪色，工业于是改造它；衍生物保住了绿色，却不再做捕光的工作。

senses.title: Porphyrin comparison
senses.titleCN: 卟啉对照：与血红素同一个环
senses.definition: the ring structure that the pigment shares with haem, differing in the central metal
senses.definitionCN: 叶绿素与血红素共有的卟啉环结构，只在中位金属上不同
senses.example: Chlorophyll and haem share a ring, but one holds magnesium.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿素与血红素共用一个环，只是其中一个装的是镁。
senses.why: Both molecules are built on a porphyrin ring; the central atom decides whether the result is green or red.
senses.whyCN: 两个分子都建在卟啉环上；中位原子决定结果偏绿还是偏红。

senses.title: Algal indicator
senses.titleCN: 水质指标：用含量判断藻华
senses.definition: the concentration used as an index of algal abundance in water
senses.definitionCN: 把叶绿素浓度当作水体藻类数量的指标
senses.example: High chlorophyll in summer points to an algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季叶绿素偏高说明发生了藻华。
senses.why: Water managers cannot count every cell, so they measure the pigment instead and let it stand for the algae.
senses.whyCN: 水质管理者数不清每一个细胞，于是改测色素，用色素代表藻类。

intro.en: Chlorophyll is a nineteenth-century scientific compound of two Greek words: pale green and leaf.
intro.cn: chlorophyll 是十九世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊词构成：淡绿与叶。

items.en: Greek chlōros meant 'pale green, greenish-yellow', and it also names Chloris, the goddess of flowers.
items.cn: 希腊 chlōros 意为「淡绿、黄绿」，它也是花神克洛里斯名字的来源。

items.en: Greek phyllon meant 'leaf', and it builds words such as phyllotaxis, the arrangement of leaves.
items.cn: 希腊 phyllon 意为「叶」，它构成 phyllotaxis（叶序）这类词。

items.en: The pigment was named by the French chemists Pelletier and Caventou in 1818, after they isolated the green matter of leaves.
items.cn: 这种色素由法国化学家佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图在 1818 年分离出叶中绿色物质之后命名。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry showed that the pigment is a porphyrin ring with magnesium at its centre, close in structure to haem.
items.cn: 二十世纪的化学表明，这种色素是中心带镁的卟啉环，结构与血红素相近。

items.en: In the twentieth century the pigment and its copper derivative entered the food and pharmaceutical colour lists.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这种色素及其铜衍生物进入了食品与药品的着色剂清单。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the name is generally attributed to Pelletier and Caventou in 1818, but the exact manuscript date is approximate; the Greek roots are certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：命名一般认为出自佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图 1818 年的工作，但确切手稿年代只是约数；希腊词根是确定的。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built with the same Greek pieces; group two holds the other leaf pigments.
note.cn: 第一组区分用相同希腊部件拼出的形近词；第二组列出叶片中的其他色素。

entries.definition: Green plus plastos 'formed': the organelle that holds the pigment, not the pigment itself.
entries.definitionCN: 绿加 plastos「成形」：装着这种色素的细胞器，而不是色素本身。

entries.definition: Green plus -osis: a condition in which leaves lose their green, from iron shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 绿加 -osis：叶片失绿的症状，常因缺铁。

entries.definition: The adjective: bearing chlorophyll, said of tissue or cells.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：含叶绿素的，用于组织或细胞。

entries.definition: Phyllon 'leaf' plus taxis 'arrangement': leaf order on a stem, with no pigment involved.
entries.definitionCN: phyllon「叶」加 taxis「排列」：茎上的叶序，与色素无关。

entries.definition: An orange-yellow pigment that also helps capture light; it passes energy to chlorophyll.
entries.definitionCN: 一种橙黄色色素，也参与捕光，并把能量传给叶绿素。

entries.definition: A water-soluble pigment making red and blue colours in leaves and fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 水溶性色素，使叶与果呈现红蓝色。

entries.definition: The oxygen-carrying blood protein; its haem group is a porphyrin ring like chlorophyll's.
entries.definitionCN: 运氧的血液蛋白；其血红素基团是与叶绿素相似的卟啉环。

entries.definition: Any substance that gives colour; chlorophyll is one pigment among many.
entries.definitionCN: 任何显色物质；叶绿素只是众多色素之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek pieces and the real chemistry, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用希腊部件与真实化学，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: chloro- 'pale green' + phyllon 'leaf': the green of the leaf.
normal.cn: chloro-「淡绿」加 phyllon「叶」：叶子的绿。

normal.en: The family: chlorophyllous, chlorophyllase, chlorophyllin, bacteriochlorophyll.
Fixed phrases: chlorophyll content, chlorophyll fluorescence, total chlorophyll.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：叶绿素含量、叶绿素荧光、总叶绿素。

normal.en: One ring, two metals: magnesium makes it green, iron makes haem red.
normal.cn: 一个环，两种金属：装镁是绿的，装铁是红的。

normal.en: It absorbs red and blue and reflects green, which is exactly the colour we see.
normal.cn: 它吸收红与蓝、反射绿，而绿正是我们看到的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a thin green film laid over every cell of the leaf, catching light.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片每个细胞上都铺着一层极薄的绿膜，用来接光。

abstract.en: Picture a dye that keeps working as a dye long after it has stopped catching light.
abstract.cn: 想象一种染料，早已不再捕光，却仍当着染料。

abstract.en: Picture a lake whose greenness can be read as a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个湖，它的绿可以被读成一个数。

examples.en: Chlorophyll gives the leaf its colour.
examples.cn: 叶绿素赋予叶片颜色。

examples.en: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
examples.cn: 叶绿素吸收红光与蓝光，反射绿光。

examples.en: High chlorophyll in summer points to an algal bloom.
examples.cn: 夏季叶绿素偏高说明发生了藻华。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绿（chloro）＋叶（phyll）」——让叶子发绿、替叶子接光的那种色素

root: 希腊 chlōros「淡绿、黄绿」＋ phyllon「叶」。词根清晰；命名者为佩尔蒂埃与卡旺图，1818 年，一般认为成立，确切手稿年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from substance to molecule to measurement to signal, then to its colour, its commercial forms, its chemical cousin, and finally its use as a water index.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从物质走到分子、测量、信号，再走到它的颜色、商品形式、化学近亲，最后走到作为水质指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green film spread through the leaf that takes in red and blue light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层铺在叶肉里、专收红光与蓝光的绿膜。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: the word begins as a name for a green stuff.
branches.cn: 物质：这个词最初是一种绿色东西的名字。

branches.en: COUNT: chemistry separates the variants and needs a plural.
branches.cn: 计数：化学分出变体，于是需要复数。

branches.en: READING: extracted or glowing, the pigment becomes a number or a signal.
branches.cn: 读数：被提取或被发光时，色素变成一个数或一个信号。

branches.en: OPTICS: what it takes and what it refuses explain its colour.
branches.cn: 光学：它拿什么、不要什么，解释了它的颜色。

branches.en: OUTSIDE: as dye, as derivative, as chemical cousin, as water index.
branches.cn: 叶外：作为染料、衍生物、化学近亲与水质指标。

intro.en: Chlorophyll is built from two Greek nouns; it has no Latin affixes and no Latin base word.
intro.cn: chlorophyll 由两个希腊名词构成；它没有拉丁词缀，也没有拉丁基础词。

latinIntro.en: Greek chlōros 'pale green' and phyllon 'leaf' combine directly; the family stays Greek, so no Latin entry applies.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 chlōros「淡绿」与 phyllon「叶」直接组合；这个词族保持希腊来源，没有适用的拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 它开启许多与绿色有关的词。

items.example: The bare stem carries only the colour.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干只带颜色义。

items.example: The noun names the organ, not the pigment.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名器官，不命名色素。
这个复合词于 1818 年造出。

items.example: The suffix names a prepared substance.

items.meaning: the bacterial form of the pigment
items.example: The prefix marks the bacterial source.

items.meaning: a loss of green in leaves
items.example: The medical suffix names a condition.
items.exampleCN: 医学后缀命名一种症状。

definition_zh: n. 合唱团，唱诗班；（教堂的）唱诗班席位
definition_en: a group of singers who perform together, especially in a church; the part of a church where they sit
core_image: 管风琴声里一排人同时起身
scene: 教堂里，唱诗班在管风琴声中起唱。The choir rose as the organ began.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：choir 指唱诗班；句意是唱诗班在管风琴声中起身演唱。

senses.title: The singing group
senses.definition: a group of singers who sing together, especially in church
senses.definitionCN: 一起演唱的歌手团体，尤指教堂中
senses.example: The choir sang a short anthem.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班唱了一首短赞美诗。
senses.why: Latin chorus came from Greek khoros, a dancing and singing group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 chorus 来自希腊语 khoros，指歌舞队。

senses.title: Their place in the church
senses.definition: the area of a church where the choir sits
senses.definitionCN: 教堂中唱诗班就座的位置
senses.example: The choir stalls were carved from oak.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班席位由橡木雕成。
senses.why: The group gave its name to the seats it used.
senses.whyCN: 这个团体把名字给了它使用的座位。

intro.en: Choir descends from Greek khoros, a group that sang and danced, through Latin chorus.
intro.cn: choir 源自希腊语 khoros（歌舞队），经拉丁语 chorus 而来。

items.en: Khoros names a dancing and singing group.
items.cn: khoros 指歌舞队。

items.en: Chorus keeps the group and its song.
items.cn: 拉丁语 chorus 兼指群体与歌声。

items.en: The French form drops into English church use.
items.cn: 古法语形式进入英语教会用语。

items.en: Choir names the church singers.
items.cn: 十四世纪指教堂歌手。

items.en: The spelling choir is fixed by scholars.
items.cn: 十七世纪学者固定拼写为 choir。

items.en: Choir also names the seats.
items.cn: 现代也指唱诗班席位。

note.en: The look-alike group is spelled close to choir; the near-meaning group names singing bodies.
note.cn: 形近组与 choir 拼写相近；近义组列出演唱团体。

normalIntro.en: A choir is a group that answers the organ with one voice.
normalIntro.cn: 唱诗班是用一个声音回应管风琴的团体。

normal.en: Greek khoros was a dancing group.
normal.cn: 希腊语 khoros 是歌舞队。

normal.en: Latin chorus kept the singers.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 chorus 保留了歌者之意。

normal.en: Church use made it a choir.
normal.cn: 教会用法把它变成唱诗班。

normal.en: The spelling hides the sound.
The stalls are named after them too.

abstract.en: Many throats, one line.
A staircase of voices.
Stone seats and living music.

examples.en: The choir rehearses on Thursday evenings.
examples.cn: 唱诗班每周四晚上排练。

examples.en: A boys choir sang before the sermon.
examples.cn: 布道前男童合唱团献唱。

examples.en: She joined the choir at fourteen.
examples.cn: 她十四岁加入合唱团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「快俄」——快看，唱诗班在俄式穹顶下起唱。

root: 希腊语 khoros（歌舞队）→ 拉丁语 chorus → 古法语 → 英语 choir

sensesIntro.en: The singers and the oak seats they fill carry the same old name.
sensesIntro.cn: 歌者与他们坐的橡木席位共用同一个古老名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of singers rising together under an organ
core.cn: 核心意象：管风琴下同时起身的一排歌者

branches.en: Robes rustling as the row stands.
branches.cn: 一排人起身时袍子的窸窣。

branches.en: A single note held by many voices.
branches.cn: 许多声音托住的一个音。

branches.en: Carved oak seats facing each other.
branches.cn: 相对而设的雕花橡木座。

branches.en: Hymn books left on a ledge.
branches.cn: 留在台沿上的赞美诗集。

branches.en: A group and the place built for it.
branches.cn: 一个团体与为它而建的座位。

intro.en: Choir is a Greek loan; the list below adds words of singing and groups.
intro.cn: choir 是希腊借词；下面列出歌唱与群体词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek khoros is a dancing group and Latin cantare is to sing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 khoros 指歌舞队，拉丁语 cantare 意为歌唱。

items.exampleCN: 唱诗班成员；唱诗班成员（复数）

latinEntries.exampleCN: chorus 产生 choir 与 chorus。
cantare 产生 chant 与 cantata。

latinEntries.example: Khoros is the source of chorus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: khoros 是 chorus 的来源。

definition_zh: 使窒息；噎住；阻塞；哽咽
definition_en: to be unable to breathe because something blocks the throat, to block a passage, or to lose the voice with strong feeling
core_image: 一只手按住喉咙，气卡在中间上不来
scene: 餐桌旁忽然静了，孩子捂着喉咙站起来。He began to choke on a piece of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 choke 指「噎住」（第 1 个义项：有东西卡在喉咙而无法呼吸）；句意是他被一块面包噎住了。

derivatives.zh: 令人窒息的东西；贴颈项链

senses.title: To block the throat
senses.definition: to be unable to breathe because something blocks the throat
senses.definitionCN: 因有东西堵住喉咙而无法呼吸
senses.example: He began to choke on a fish bone.
senses.exampleCN: 他被一根鱼刺噎住了。
senses.why: The Old English word named the jaw and the throat, the very place where breath is stopped.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指颌与喉，正是呼吸被阻断的地方。

senses.title: To block a passage
senses.definition: to block or fill a passage so that things cannot move through
senses.definitionCN: 堵住通道，使东西无法通过
senses.example: Weeds choked the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 杂草堵塞了狭窄的水道。
senses.why: A blocked throat and a blocked channel share the same image of something jammed tight.
senses.whyCN: 喉咙被堵与通道被堵共享同一个死死卡住的意象。

senses.title: To lose the voice with feeling
senses.definition: to be unable to speak clearly because of strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 因情绪强烈而说不清话
senses.example: She choked back her tears and went on.
senses.exampleCN: 她强忍眼泪继续说了下去。
senses.why: Tears tighten the throat, so the word for the throat came to mean speech stopped by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 泪水使喉咙发紧，于是这个喉咙词也指被情绪堵住的话。

intro.en: Choke began as an Old English word for the jaw and the throat.
intro.cn: choke 原本是古英语中指颌与喉的词。

items.en: A root keuk- named the jaw and the swallowing throat.
items.cn: 词根 keuk- 指颌骨与吞咽的喉咙。

items.en: Aceocian meant to choke, beside ceoce for the jaw.
items.cn: aceocian 意为窒息，旁边还有 ceoce 指颌。

items.en: Choken narrowed to the stoppage of breath.
items.cn: choken 的词义收窄为呼吸受阻。

items.en: The same verb spread to blocked pipes and blocked roads.
items.cn: 同一个动词扩展到堵塞的管道与道路。

items.en: The throat image produced the sense of speech stopped by emotion.
items.cn: 喉咙的意象又生出被情绪堵住话的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch sound, while the meaning group names ways of stopping breath.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch 音，近义组列出各种使呼吸停滞的说法。

entries.definition: the soft side of the face below the eye
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛下方柔软的面部侧面

entries.definition: a group of people who sing together
a building used for Christian worship
entries.definitionCN: 用于基督教礼拜的建筑

entries.definition: to die or suffer from lack of air
to kill by pressing hard on the throat

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw origin, the throat image and the three everyday phrase families.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌骨来源、喉咙意象以及三组日常搭配。

normal.en: Choke and cheek are cousins: the throat that chokes sits right beside the cheek.
normal.cn: choke 与 cheek 是亲戚：噎住的喉咙就在脸颊旁边。

normal.en: Choke on food, choke back tears, choke off supplies: the particle shows what is blocked.
normal.cn: choke on food、choke back tears、choke off supplies，小品词标出被堵住的东西。

normal.en: A choked voice is a throat tightened by feeling, not by food.
normal.cn: a choked voice 是被情绪而非食物勒紧的喉咙。

normal.en: A drain choked with leaves repeats the blocked channel sense exactly.
normal.cn: a drain choked with leaves 完全重复了通道堵塞那一义。

normal.en: The noun choke names the sound and the valve that cuts off air.
normal.cn: 名词 choke 指那种声音，也指截断空气的阀门。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rising to a throat in the middle of a meal.
abstract.cn: 想象吃饭吃到一半，一只手猛地捂上喉咙。

abstract.en: Picture weeds packed so tight that water cannot pass.
abstract.cn: 想象杂草挤得密不透风，水一点也过不去。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker stopping mid sentence with shining eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象说话的人眼睛发亮，话说到一半停住。

examples.en: The thick smoke made him choke.
examples.cn: 浓烟呛得他喘不上气。

examples.en: Anger choked his words for a moment.
examples.cn: 愤怒让他一时说不出话。

examples.en: The drain was choked with wet leaves.
examples.cn: 排水口被湿叶子堵住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: choke 与 cheek 同源：卡住的正是紧挨脸颊的那段喉咙。

root: 源自古英语 aceocian（窒息），与 ceoce（颌、颊）同源，本指喉咙被堵住而无法呼吸。

sensesIntro.en: A blocked throat gives the bodily sense, which spreads to blocked passages and then to speech stopped by feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 喉咙被堵给出身体义，随后扩展到堵塞的通道，再扩展到被情绪堵住的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath stuck halfway down a narrowed throat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气卡在收窄的喉咙中间。

branches.en: Food in the throat stops the breath at once.
branches.cn: 食物卡在喉里，呼吸立刻停住。

branches.en: Pipes and roads repeat the same jam on a larger scale.
branches.cn: 管道与道路把同一种堵塞放大到更大范围。

branches.en: Tears press on the throat until words fail.
branches.cn: 泪水压住喉咙，直到话语出不来。

branches.en: Body and feeling both tighten the same passage.
branches.cn: 身体与情绪收紧的是同一条通道。

branches.en: Throat and channel share one verb of blocking.
branches.cn: 喉咙与通道共用一个表示堵塞的动词。

intro.en: The short stem choke carries the verb, its inflections and two compound nouns.
intro.cn: 短词干 choke 支撑动词、各种屈折形式以及两个复合名词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin: Old English ceoce for the jaw lies behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，背后是古英语 ceoce（颌）。

items.example: He chokes whenever he eats too fast.
items.exampleCN: 他每次吃得太快都会噎住。

items.example: The dust was choking the workers.
items.exampleCN: 灰尘呛得工人喘不过气。

items.meaning: a thing that chokes or a tight necklace
items.meaningCN: 令人窒息之物或贴颈项链
items.exampleCN: 她戴着一条黑色贴颈项链。

items.meaning: a thing or person that acts

latinEntries.example: Ceoce is the old jaw word behind choke.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceoce 是 choke 背后的古颌骨词。

definition_zh: n. 胆固醇
definition_en: a fatty substance found in the body and in some foods, linked to heart disease when too high
core_image: 化验单上一行偏高的数字
scene: 医生说他的胆固醇偏高，要少吃油炸食品。The doctor said his cholesterol was high.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cholesterol 指胆固醇；句意是医生说他的胆固醇偏高。

senses.title: The blood measure
senses.definition: the level of this fatty substance in the blood, watched by doctors
senses.definitionCN: 血液中这种脂肪物质的水平，医生会监测
senses.example: His cholesterol fell after the diet change.
senses.exampleCN: 改变饮食后他的胆固醇下降了。
senses.why: The word was coined for a solid fat found in gallstones.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指胆结石中发现的一种固体脂肪。

senses.title: The substance in food
senses.definition: the fatty substance present in foods such as eggs and meat
senses.definitionCN: 鸡蛋、肉类等食物中所含的这种脂肪物质
senses.example: Eggs are high in dietary cholesterol.
senses.exampleCN: 鸡蛋的膳食胆固醇含量较高。
senses.why: The same chemical is measured in food and in blood.
senses.whyCN: 同一种化学物质既在食物中也在血液中被测量。

intro.en: Cholesterol joins Greek khole, bile, stereos, solid, and the alcohol ending -ol.
intro.cn: cholesterol 由希腊语 khole（胆汁）、stereos（固体）与表示醇的词尾 -ol 组成。

items.en: Khole means bile.
items.cn: khole 意为胆汁。

items.en: Stereos means solid.
items.cn: stereos 意为固体。

items.en: The name is coined for a fat in gallstones.
items.cn: 1815 年为胆结石中的一种脂肪命名。

items.en: The ending -ol marks it as an alcohol.
items.cn: 十九世纪词尾 -ol 标明它是醇。

items.en: Cholesterol is linked to heart disease.
items.cn: 二十世纪胆固醇与心脏病联系起来。

items.en: The word names a routine blood measure.
items.cn: 现代指常规血液指标。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chol- opening; the near-meaning group names blood fats.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chol- 开头；近义组列出血脂相关词。

entries.definition: A solid alcohol found in fats.
A common fat carried in blood.

normalIntro.en: A solid fat from bile that doctors now watch in the blood.
normalIntro.cn: 一种来自胆汁的固体脂肪，如今医生在血里监测它。

normal.en: Khole means bile.
Stereos means solid.
-ol marks an alcohol.
It was first found in gallstones.
normal.cn: 它最初在胆结石中被发现。

normal.en: High levels worry the heart.

abstract.en: A number with a diet attached.
Wax in the pipes of the body.
Chemistry read as a warning.

examples.en: His cholesterol is slightly above normal.
examples.cn: 他的胆固醇略高于正常值。

examples.en: Oily fish can help lower cholesterol.
examples.cn: 多脂鱼有助于降低胆固醇。

examples.en: The clinic offers a free cholesterol test.
examples.cn: 诊所提供免费胆固醇检测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隔死特罗」——胆固醇高了，血管隔得死，特别难过。

root: 希腊语 khole（胆汁）+ stereos（固体）+ -ol（醇）→ cholesterol

sensesIntro.en: The chemical is the same; one sense is the blood reading and one is the food label.
sensesIntro.cn: 化学物质相同，一义指血液读数，一义指食物成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed number just above the normal line
core.cn: 核心意象：化验单上略高于正常线的一个数字

branches.en: A lab sheet with a red mark.
branches.cn: 带红标记的化验单。

branches.en: A doctor tapping the printed range.
branches.cn: 医生指着打印的正常范围。

branches.en: An egg cracked into a pan.
branches.cn: 打进锅里的一个鸡蛋。

branches.en: A food label turned over.
branches.cn: 翻过来的食品标签。

branches.en: One fatty substance, two places to read it.
branches.cn: 同一种脂肪，两处读数。

intro.en: Cholesterol is built from Greek and chemical parts; the list below adds words of fat and arteries.
intro.cn: cholesterol 由希腊语与化学构件组成；下面列出脂肪与动脉词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin adeps is fat and arteria is a windpipe, later an artery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adeps 意为脂肪，arteria 原指气管，后指动脉。

latinEntries.example: Khole is the first element of cholesterol.
latinEntries.exampleCN: khole 是 cholesterol 的第一部分。
stereos 产生 stereo 与 cholesterol。
arteria 产生 artery 与 arterial。

definition_zh: 砍；劈；剁；切碎；排骨
definition_en: to cut something with a heavy blow, to cut food into small pieces, or a small piece of meat cut with a rib
core_image: 一把菜刀落在砧板上，把肉剁成两半
scene: 厨房里飘着洋葱味，砧板响个不停。She chopped the onions into small pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 chopped 是 chop 的过去式，指「切碎」（第 2 个义项：把食物切成小块）；句意是她把洋葱切成了小块。

senses.title: To cut with a heavy blow
senses.definition: to cut something with a heavy blow from an axe or a large knife
senses.definitionCN: 用斧头或大刀重重砍下
senses.example: He chopped the branch off the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那根树枝从树上砍了下来。
senses.why: Middle English choppen imitated the short heavy sound of a blade striking wood.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 choppen 模仿刀刃击木时短促沉重的声音。

senses.title: To cut food small
senses.definition: to cut food into small pieces with quick heavy blows
senses.definitionCN: 用快速有力的刀法把食物切成小块
senses.example: She chopped the onions into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 她把洋葱切成了小块。
senses.why: The same short blow moved from firewood to the kitchen board.
senses.whyCN: 同样短促的砍击从木柴移到了厨房砧板。

senses.title: A piece of meat on a rib
senses.definition: a small piece of meat cut together with a rib bone
senses.definitionCN: 带肋骨一起切下的一小块肉
senses.example: We had lamb chops for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚饭吃了羊排。
senses.why: A chop is literally a piece chopped off the carcass.
senses.whyCN: chop 字面上就是从整只牲畜身上剁下来的一块。

intro.en: Chop probably began as a sound word for a short heavy blow.
intro.cn: chop 最初很可能是一个模仿短促沉重砍击的拟声词。

items.en: The shape of the word echoes a blade striking wood.
items.cn: 这个词的声音模仿刀刃击木。

items.en: Choppen meant to cut with repeated heavy blows.
items.cn: choppen 意为用反复的重击来砍。

items.en: The verb spread from firewood to meat and vegetables.
items.cn: 这个动词从木柴扩展到肉类与蔬菜。

items.en: The noun named a rib piece cut off the carcass.
items.cn: 名词指从整只牲畜上剁下的带骨肉块。

items.en: Compounds gave chopsticks, chopper and the adjective choppy.
items.cn: 复合构词又生出 chopsticks、chopper 与形容词 choppy。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the short ch spelling, while the meaning group names ways of cutting.
note.cn: 形近组保持短促的 ch 拼写，近义组列出各种切割方式。

entries.definition: a small piece broken off something
a place where goods are sold
to crack or redden from cold
to divide something with a blade
to cut into thin flat pieces
to cut food into very small bits
entries.definitionCN: 把食物切成极小的碎末

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the sound of the blade, the kitchen board and the meat sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刀声、厨房砧板以及排骨义。

normal.en: Say chop twice quickly and you hear an axe on a log.
normal.cn: 快速连说两次 chop，就听见斧头落在木头上的声音。

normal.en: Chop wood is the wood sense, chop onions is the kitchen sense, and both are short blows.
normal.cn: chop wood 是劈柴义，chop onions 是厨房义，两者都是短促的砍击。

normal.en: A pork chop is a piece chopped off, so the noun keeps the verb image.
normal.cn: a pork chop 就是剁下来的一块，名词保留了动词的意象。

normal.en: Chop down adds down, and the tree falls in the direction of the blow.
normal.cn: chop down 加上 down，树便朝砍击的方向倒下。

normal.en: Chopsticks and chopper both start from the same short stem.
normal.cn: chopsticks 与 chopper 都从同一个短词干出发。

abstract.en: Picture a blade biting into a log with a dull thud.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃咬进木头，发出一声闷响。

abstract.en: Picture a board covered with neat piles of diced onion.
abstract.cn: 想象砧板上是一小堆一小堆切好的洋葱丁。

abstract.en: Picture a thick chop bone showing at the edge of the meat.
abstract.cn: 想象肉块边缘露出一截粗大的骨头。

examples.en: He chopped wood for the fire all morning.
examples.cn: 他整个上午都在劈柴生火。

examples.en: Add two chopped carrots to the pot.
examples.cn: 往锅里加两根切碎的胡萝卜。

examples.en: The pork chop was thick and juicy.
examples.cn: 那块猪排又厚又多汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: chop 读起来就像刀落砧板的一声：剁。

root: 源自中古英语 choppen（砍、剁），可能模仿刀斧砍击的声音，与 chap 相关。

sensesIntro.en: A short heavy blow gives the cutting sense, which moves to the kitchen and then to the piece of meat cut off.
sensesIntro.cn: 短促的重击先给出砍的动作，再移到厨房，最后指剁下来的那块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade falling once on a wooden board.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃在木板上落下一次。

branches.en: The axe sense is the oldest and the most physical.
branches.cn: 斧头义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: The same blow works on onions and carrots.
branches.cn: 同样的砍击用在洋葱与胡萝卜上。

branches.en: The noun names the piece that the blow leaves.
branches.cn: 名词指这一刀之后留下的那块肉。

branches.en: Wood and food share one verb of short strokes.
branches.cn: 木柴与食物共用一个短促下刀的动词。

branches.en: The cut food and the cut meat sit side by side.
branches.cn: 切好的菜与剁下的肉彼此相邻。

intro.en: The short stem chop carries the verb, its inflections and three familiar compounds.
intro.cn: 短词干 chop 支撑动词、各种屈折形式以及三个常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and partly imitative, so no Latin root is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语且带拟声成分，不涉及拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to cut with a heavy blow

items.example: The chopper hung by the stove.
The lake was choppy that day.
He ate the noodles with chopsticks.

items.meaning: a tool or person that acts

latinEntries.example: Choppen is the recorded source of chop.
latinEntries.exampleCN: choppen 是 chop 有记录的来源。

definition_zh: n. 和弦；（几何、解剖）弦；心弦
definition_en: a group of notes played together; a straight line joining two points on a curve
core_image: 三根手指同时按下琴键
scene: 他随手按下三个琴键，弹出一个柔和的和弦。He pressed three keys and struck a soft chord.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chord 指和弦；句意是他按下三个琴键弹出一个柔和的和弦。

senses.title: Notes sounded together
senses.definition: three or more notes played at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时奏出的三个或更多音
senses.example: A minor chord closed the song.
senses.exampleCN: 一首小调和弦收尾。
senses.why: Latin chorda meant a string, and strings make chords.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 chorda 意为弦，而弦发出和弦。

senses.title: A line across a curve
senses.definition: a straight line joining two points on a circle or curve
senses.definitionCN: 连接圆或曲线上两点的直线
senses.example: The chord cuts the circle into two parts.
senses.exampleCN: 这条弦把圆分成两部分。
senses.why: The geometric sense is the older, literal one.
senses.whyCN: 几何义是更早、更字面的含义。

intro.en: Chord comes from Latin chorda, a string, from Greek khorde.
intro.cn: chord 来自拉丁语 chorda（弦），源自希腊语 khorde。

items.en: Khorde means a string of gut.
items.cn: khorde 意为肠弦。

items.en: Chorda keeps the string sense.
items.cn: chorda 保留「弦」的含义。

items.en: English uses chord for string and note.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语兼指弦与音。

items.en: The spelling chord marks the musical sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪拼写 chord 标记音乐义。

items.en: Chord names a group of notes.
items.cn: 十八世纪指一组同时发声的音。

definition_zh: 染色体；细胞中承载基因的线状结构
definition_en: a thread-like structure of DNA and protein in the cell nucleus that carries genes
core_image: 一团细线被压缩成一对可以辨形的棒状物
scene: 显微镜下，细胞核里的细线排成一列。Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21.
sceneCN: 这里 chromosome 指「染色体」（第 1 个义项：细胞核中承载基因的线状结构）；句意：唐氏综合征由第 21 号染色体多出一份引起。

pos.zh: 染色体；（细菌的）环状染色体

senses.title: Gene carrier
senses.definition: a structure of DNA and protein that carries the genes of a cell
senses.definitionCN: 由 DNA 与蛋白质构成、承载细胞基因的结构
senses.example: Humans have forty-six chromosomes in most body cells.
senses.exampleCN: 人类大多数体细胞有四十六条染色体。
senses.why: Chroma named the colour seen under early dyes and soma named the body; the compound literally means a coloured body, which is what a stained chromosome looks like.
senses.whyCN: chroma 指早期染料下看到的颜色，soma 指身体；复合词字面就是「有色的物体」，这正是染色后染色体的样子。

senses.title: Visible during division
senses.definition: the condensed form of chromatin that becomes visible when a cell divides
senses.definitionCN: 染色质在细胞分裂时凝缩而成的可见形态
senses.example: Chromosomes line up along the middle of the cell before separating.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体在分开之前沿细胞中央排成一行。
senses.why: Only during division does the material condense enough to be seen as distinct bodies, so the word names that visible stage.
senses.whyCN: 只有在分裂时，这些物质才凝缩到能被看成独立小体的程度，因此这个词命名的是那个可见阶段。

senses.title: Carrier of heredity
senses.definition: the physical vehicle by which genes pass from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 基因由亲代传给子代的物理载体
senses.example: Each parent contributes one chromosome of every pair.
senses.exampleCN: 每一对染色体中，父母各贡献一条。
senses.why: Once genes were located on these bodies, the chromosome became the vehicle of inheritance rather than only a stained object.
senses.whyCN: 基因被定位到这些小体上之后，染色体就从「被染色的物体」变成了遗传的载体。

senses.title: Sex chromosomes
senses.definition: the pair, X and Y, that determines biological sex in many animals
senses.definitionCN: 在许多动物中决定生物学性别的 X 与 Y 这一对
senses.example: A single chromosome decides whether the embryo develops testes.
senses.exampleCN: 一条染色体就决定了胚胎是否发育出睾丸。
senses.why: One pair carries the sex-determining genes, so the word is used in the singular when the identity of that chromosome matters.
senses.whyCN: 有一对染色体携带决定性别的基因，因此当重要的是那一条的身份时，这个词会用单数。

senses.title: Chromosome number
senses.definition: the characteristic count of chromosomes in a species
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种特有的染色体条数
senses.example: The chromosome number of a species is usually constant.
senses.exampleCN: 一个物种的染色体数目通常是恒定的。
senses.why: Because the count is species-typical, the word participates in a standard measurement rather than in a physical description.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个数目是物种的典型特征，这个词参与的是一项标准测量，而不是物理描述。

senses.title: Chromosome abnormality
senses.definition: a change in chromosome number or structure that affects development
senses.definitionCN: 染色体数目或结构的改变，影响发育
senses.example: The test looks for a chromosome abnormality in the fetus.
senses.exampleCN: 这项检查寻找胎儿的染色体异常。
senses.why: Since chromosomes hold the instructions, a change in their number or shape is a change in the instructions.
senses.whyCN: 既然染色体保存着指令，那么数目或形状的改变就是指令的改变。

senses.title: Bacterial chromosome
senses.definition: the usually circular DNA molecule of a bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 细菌通常呈环状的 DNA 分子
senses.example: The bacterial chromosome replicates before the cell divides.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌染色体在细胞分裂之前复制。
senses.why: Bacteria keep their DNA in one loop without a nucleus, and the word is stretched to cover this simpler arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 细菌把 DNA 放在一个没有细胞核的环里，这个词被延伸来涵盖这种更简单的安排。

senses.title: Chromosome in a karyotype
senses.definition: a single chromosome as displayed, counted and identified in a karyotype
senses.definitionCN: 在核型图中被展示、计数并识别的一条染色体
senses.example: The karyotype showed one chromosome with an unusual banding pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 核型图显示有一条染色体的带型异常。
senses.why: Once chromosomes are photographed and arranged in pairs, each one becomes an identifiable item in a standard display, and the word names that item.
senses.whyCN: 当染色体被拍摄并按对排列后，每一条都成为标准展示中的可识别项，这个词就命名那个项。

intro.en: Chromosome is a Greek compound coined in 19th-century German microscopy: colour plus body.
intro.cn: chromosome 是 19 世纪德国显微学造出的希腊语复合词：颜色加身体。

items.en: Greek chroma meant colour, and chrōma was also used for the skin or surface colour. The element chrom- later gave words like chromium and monochrome.
items.cn: 希腊语 chroma 指颜色，chrōma 也用于皮肤或表面颜色。成分 chrom- 后来衍生出 chromium、monochrome 等词。

items.en: Greek sōma meant body, as opposed to soul or to a part. It survives in somatic, psychosomatic and chromosome.
items.cn: 希腊语 sōma 指身体，与灵魂或局部相对。它保留在 somatic、psychosomatic、chromosome 中。

items.en: The German anatomist Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz is generally credited with the term Chromosom in 1888, naming the bodies that take up dye during division. The attribution is widely accepted but the exact first printed use is debated.
items.cn: 德国解剖学家 Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz 一般认为在 1888 年创造了 Chromosom 一词，用来指分裂时能吸收染料的那些小体。归属被广泛接受，但确切的首见印刷用例仍有争议。

items.en: Once chromosomes were tied to Mendelian inheritance, the word moved from cytology to genetics.
items.cn: 染色体与孟德尔遗传规律联系起来之后，这个词从细胞学进入遗传学。

items.en: The human chromosome number was established as 46 in 1956, correcting an earlier figure of 48.
items.cn: 人类染色体数目在 1956 年被确定为 46 条，纠正了此前 48 条的结论。

note.en: The first group separates chromosome from the materials and structures inside it; the second separates it from the units that carry genes at a different scale.
note.cn: 第一组把 chromosome 与它内部的物质和结构分开；第二组把它与在别的尺度上承载基因的单元分开。

entries.definition: The complex of DNA and protein as it exists between divisions; when it condenses into visible bodies, those bodies are chromosomes.
entries.definitionCN: 指分裂间期 DNA 与蛋白质的复合物；当它凝缩成可见小体时，那些小体才是染色体。

entries.definition: One of the two identical strands of a chromosome after copying; the two chromatids together make one chromosome.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制后染色体中两条相同丝状物之一；两条染色单体合起来才算一条染色体。

entries.definition: The adjective for 'of chromosomes'; it modifies abnormality, location or mapping, while chromosome is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「染色体的」，修饰 abnormality、location、mapping 等；chromosome 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A segment of DNA that codes for a product; a chromosome is a long molecule carrying many genes.
entries.definitionCN: 指编码产物的 DNA 片段；一条染色体是携带许多基因的长分子。

entries.definition: The complete set of genetic material of an organism; chromosomes are the physical packages in which it is stored.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个生物的全部遗传物质；染色体是储存这些物质的物理包装。

entries.definition: A small circular DNA molecule separate from the bacterial chromosome, often carrying drug-resistance genes.
entries.definitionCN: 指细菌中独立于染色体的小型环状 DNA 分子，常携带抗药基因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: chroma 'colour' + soma 'body': the coloured body seen under the microscope.
normal.cn: chroma「颜色」+ soma「身体」：显微镜下那个被染上颜色的小体。

normal.en: The family runs chromosomal, chromatin, chromatid and chromosome mapping.
Fixed phrases: sex chromosome, X chromosome, chromosome number, extra chromosome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：性染色体、X 染色体、染色体数目、多余染色体。

normal.en: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.
normal.cn: 人类有 46 条染色体，共 23 对。

normal.en: A chromosome is a library shelf; a gene is one book on it.
normal.cn: 染色体像一排书架，基因是架上的一本书。

abstract.en: Picture a very long thread wound tight until it looks like a short thick rod.
abstract.cn: 想象一根很长的线被紧紧缠绕，直到看起来像一根短粗的棒。

abstract.en: A stained chromosome is a suspect lit up under a lamp: the dye reveals what was invisible.
abstract.cn: 染色后的染色体像灯下被照亮的嫌疑人：染料让原本看不见的东西显形。

abstract.en: An extra chromosome is one duplicate page bound into a manual.
abstract.cn: 多出一条染色体，就像手册里多装订了一页副本。

examples.en: Each human cell usually contains 23 pairs of chromosomes.
examples.cn: 每个人类细胞通常含有 23 对染色体。

examples.en: The extra chromosome 21 is the cause of Down syndrome.
examples.cn: 多出的第 21 号染色体是唐氏综合征的成因。

examples.en: Chromosomes must be copied and separated precisely before a cell divides.
examples.cn: 细胞分裂前，染色体必须被精确复制并分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chromo（颜色）+ some（体）」→ 染色后显形的「有色小体」→ 染色体

root: 希腊语 chroma「颜色」+ sōma「身体」→ 德语 Chromosom（1888 年 Waldeyer 提出）→ 英语 chromosome。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the gene-carrying body to its visible form, its role in heredity, the sex pair, the species count, the abnormality, the bacterial loop, and finally the single chromosome as it is displayed and identified in a karyotype.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「承载基因的小体」出发，经过它可见的形态、遗传作用、性染色体、物种数目、异常、细菌环状 DNA，最后到核型图中被展示并识别的那一条染色体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long thread folded into a compact rod that takes up dye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长线折叠成能吸收染料的紧凑短棒。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the gene carrier as a structure, and the condensed form in which it becomes visible.
branches.cn: 对象：作为结构的基因载体，以及使它变得可见的凝缩形态。

branches.en: INHERITANCE: the vehicle from parents to offspring, including the pair that sets sex.
branches.cn: 遗传：从亲代到子代的载体，包括决定性别的那一对。

branches.en: COUNT: the species-typical number becomes a measurable property.
branches.cn: 数目：物种特有的条数成为可测量的属性。

branches.en: ERROR: an abnormal count or shape changes the instructions.
branches.cn: 错误：数目或形状异常会改变指令。

branches.en: SIMPLER FORMS: the bacterial loop and the single chromosome as it appears in a karyotype.
branches.cn: 更简单的形态：细菌的环状 DNA，以及核型图中出现的那一条染色体。

intro.en: Chromosome is a Greek-Greek compound with no English affix; its parts are still transparent in scientific vocabulary.
intro.cn: chromosome 是希腊语与希腊语的复合词，不含英语词缀；它的成分在科学词汇中仍然透明。

latinIntro.en: Both elements are Greek: chroma for colour and sōma for body. Latin plays no part, though the word was coined in German scientific Latin and reached English through it.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都来自希腊语：chroma 表颜色，sōma 表身体。拉丁语没有参与构词，但这个词是在德语科学拉丁语环境中造出，再经其进入英语。

items.example: The chromosome carries hundreds of genes.
items.exampleCN: 这条染色体携带数百个基因。

items.example: Chromosomal DNA is stored in the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 染色体 DNA 储存在细胞核中。

items.meaningCN: 构成染色体的 DNA 与蛋白质物质
items.example: Chromatin loosens in the active regions.
items.exampleCN: 染色质在活跃区域会变得松散。

items.meaning: one strand of a copied chromosome
items.meaningCN: 复制后染色体的一条丝
items.example: Each chromatid is pulled to a pole.
items.exampleCN: 每条染色单体被拉向一极。

items.meaning: separation of substances by colour bands
items.meaningCN: 按色带分离物质的方法
items.exampleCN: 层析法把色素分离开来。

items.example: Somatic cells do not form gametes.

items.meaning: a chromosome other than a sex chromosome
items.meaningCN: 除性染色体之外的染色体
items.exampleCN: 人类有 22 对常染色体。

items.example: The genome is split across chromosomes.
items.exampleCN: 基因组分布在多条染色体上。

items.meaning: the protective end of a chromosome
items.meaningCN: 染色体末端的保护结构
items.exampleCN: 端粒随着每次分裂而缩短。

latinEntries.meaning: a body, as opposed to a soul or part
latinEntries.meaningCN: 身体（相对于灵魂或局部）

latinEntries.meaning: used in compounds for a body or particle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用于复合词，表示身体或小体

definition_zh: adj. 慢性的；（问题）长期的；积习难改的
definition_en: lasting a long time and hard to cure; happening again and again over a long period
core_image: 病历上连续几年的同一行诊断
scene: 他有多年的腰痛，属于慢性问题。He has had back pain for years, a chronic problem.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chronic 指慢性的；句意是他多年的腰痛属于慢性问题。

senses.title: Long-lasting illness
senses.definition: of an illness that lasts a long time and is hard to cure
senses.definitionCN: 指病程长、难以治愈的疾病
senses.example: She has chronic asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 她患有慢性哮喘。
senses.why: Greek khronikos means of time, from khronos, time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 khronikos 意为与时间有关的，源自 khronos（时间）。

senses.title: A long-running problem
senses.definition: continuing for a long time and difficult to solve
senses.definitionCN: 持续很久且难以解决的
senses.example: The city has a chronic housing shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市长期住房短缺。
senses.why: The medical sense widened to any long habit or problem.
senses.whyCN: 医学义扩大到任何长期习惯或问题。

intro.en: Chronic comes from Greek khronikos, of time, from khronos, time.
intro.cn: chronic 来自希腊语 khronikos（与时间有关的），源自 khronos（时间）。

items.en: Khronos means time.
items.cn: khronos 意为时间。

items.en: Khronikos means of time.
items.cn: khronikos 意为与时间有关的。

items.en: English uses chronic for long illness.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语指病程长的病。

items.en: Chronic comes to mean long-standing.
items.cn: 十七世纪泛指长期存在的。

items.en: Chronic also describes fixed habits.
items.cn: 十九世纪也形容积习。

items.en: The word pairs with acute in medicine.
items.cn: 现代在医学上与 acute 相对。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chron- root; the near-meaning group pairs long with short.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chron- 词根；近义组把长期与短期并置。

entries.definition: The order of events in time.

normalIntro.en: Chronos is time, so chronic means the thing time refuses to cure.
normalIntro.cn: chronos 是时间，chronic 就是时间不肯治愈的那件事。

normal.en: Khronos means time.
Chronic means of time.
normal.cn: chronic 意为与时间有关的。

normal.en: A chronic illness lasts and lasts.
A chronic shortage never quite ends.
normal.cn: 长期短缺总也结束不了。

normal.en: Its opposite is acute.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 acute（急性的）。

abstract.en: A calendar that will not close.
Pain with a long address.
The slowest kind of emergency.

examples.en: Chronic pain changed the way he sat.
examples.cn: 慢性疼痛改变了他的坐姿。

examples.en: The hospital treats chronic as well as acute cases.
examples.cn: 这家医院既治急性也治慢性病例。

examples.en: Chronic delays damaged the project.
examples.cn: 长期拖延损害了这个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克朗尼克」——病拖过了几个克朗，还是慢性。

root: 希腊语 khronos（时间）→ khronikos（与时间有关的）→ 英语 chronic

sensesIntro.en: A word about time first described long illness, then any long-standing problem.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个关于时间的词先形容久病，再形容任何长期问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same diagnosis repeated on yearly records
core.cn: 核心意象：年复一年的病历上重复同一诊断

branches.en: Old prescriptions stacked in a drawer.
branches.cn: 抽屉里一叠旧处方。

branches.en: A chair adjusted for a bad back.
branches.cn: 为腰痛调过的椅子。

branches.en: A housing queue that never shrinks.
branches.cn: 从不缩短的住房排队。

branches.en: A headline returning every year.
branches.cn: 每年都回来的标题。

branches.en: Trouble measured in years.
branches.cn: 以年计量的麻烦。

intro.en: Chronic carries a Greek root for time; the list below adds words of time, order and duration.
intro.cn: chronic 含有希腊语「时间」词根；下面列出时间、顺序与持续词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek khronos is time and Latin tempus is time as well.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 khronos 意为时间，拉丁语 tempus 也意为时间。

items.exampleCN: 按时间顺序的；生物学的

latinEntries.exampleCN: khronos 产生 chronic 与 chronology。
tempus 产生 temporary 与 tempo。
aevum 产生 eternal 与 longevity。

definition_zh: 按时间顺序的；年代学的；编年的
definition_en: arranged in the order in which events happened, or relating to the study of dates and time sequences
core_image: 一条从左向右延伸的时间轴，事件像珠子一样按发生的先后串在上面
scene: 档案馆员把一叠信件摊在长桌上，按邮戳日期从最早排到最晚。The archivist spreads the letters on a long table and lays them out in chronological order by postmark date.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chronological 指按时间顺序的；句意是馆员按邮戳日期把信件从最早排到最晚。

pos.zh: 按时间顺序的；年代学的；编年的

senses.title: Arranged by time of occurrence
senses.definition: ordered from earliest to latest according to when things happened
senses.definitionCN: 按照事情发生的先后，从最早到最晚排列
senses.example: The files are kept in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 这些档案按时间顺序保存。
senses.why: Chronological answers one question only: which came first? It ignores importance, size and logic, and keeps a single axis.
senses.whyCN: chronological 只回答一个问题：哪个先发生？它不管重要性、规模与逻辑，只保留一条轴。

senses.title: Belonging to chronology as a discipline
senses.definition: relating to the science of establishing and ordering dates
senses.definitionCN: 与确定日期并排列日期的学问有关
senses.example: Chronological research fixed the date of the eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 年代学研究确定了那次日食的日期。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes a method, not an arrangement. The scholar is not sorting papers but testing whether a date can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述一种方法，而不是一种排列。学者不是在整理纸堆，而是在检验一个日期是否可信。

senses.title: Of a sequence of records or events
senses.definition: describing a series whose items follow one another in time
senses.definitionCN: 描述按时间先后相接的一系列项目
senses.example: The report gives a chronological account of the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 报告按时间顺序叙述了谈判过程。
senses.why: A chronological account follows the clock rather than the argument. The reader learns what happened next, not what mattered most.
senses.whyCN: 编年式叙述跟着时钟走，而不是跟着论点走。读者知道接下来发生了什么，而不是什么最重要。

senses.title: Of age order
senses.definition: arranged by age, as of children in a class or siblings in a family
senses.definitionCN: 按年龄排列，如班级里的孩子或家庭中的兄弟姐妹
senses.example: The children were seated in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们按年龄顺序就座。
senses.why: Age is time made visible in a body. The adjective transfers the timeline from events to people, and the order becomes a seating plan.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是时间在身体上的可见化。这个形容词把时间轴从事件移到人身上，顺序就变成了一张座位表。

senses.title: Chronological narrative form
senses.definition: a style of telling a story from beginning to end without flashbacks
senses.definitionCN: 从头到尾讲述、不使用倒叙的叙事方式
senses.example: The film's chronological structure makes it feel like a documentary.
senses.exampleCN: 影片的编年结构让它像一部纪录片。
senses.why: Storytellers usually rearrange time for effect. Calling a narrative chronological marks the absence of that rearrangement, and that absence is itself a style.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事的人通常为了效果而重排时间。称一个叙述为 chronological，标示这种重排的缺席，而这种缺席本身就是一种风格。

senses.title: Geological time order
senses.definition: relating to the order of rock layers and past geological events
senses.definitionCN: 与岩层及过去地质事件的先后有关
senses.example: Geologists established a chronological framework for the strata.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家为这些地层建立了年代框架。
senses.why: In geology the timeline is read from the ground up: lower layers are older. The adjective describes an order that the earth itself recorded.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，时间轴要从下往上读：下层更古老。这个形容词描述的是大地自己记录下来的顺序。

senses.title: Chronological representation as a timeline
senses.definition: shown on a line or chart where distance stands for elapsed time
senses.definitionCN: 在一条线或图表上呈现，用距离表示流逝的时间
senses.example: The museum uses a chronological chart from 1800 to the present.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆使用一张从 1800 年至今的时间轴图。
senses.why: A timeline turns sequence into space. Once time is drawn as length, gaps and clusters become visible at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 时间轴把先后变成空间。一旦时间被画成长度，空白与密集就一眼可见。

senses.title: Chronological age in contrast to other measures
senses.titleCN: 与其它度量相对的实龄
senses.definition: in psychology and medicine, actual years lived, as opposed to mental or biological age
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学与医学中，实际活过的年数，相对于心理年龄或生理年龄
senses.example: Her chronological age is seventy, but her biological age is closer to fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的实际年龄是七十岁，但生理年龄接近五十。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a way of separating clocks from bodies. It marks the plain calendar count so that another, less visible count can be compared with it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了一种把日历与身体分开的方式。它标出朴素的日历计数，好让另一种不那么可见的计数与之比较。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase chronological order
senses.titleCN: 用于固定搭配 chronological order
senses.definition: in the phrase in chronological order, meaning following the actual sequence of events
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in chronological order，表示依照事件的实际先后
senses.example: Please list the incidents in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 请按时间顺序列出这些事件。
senses.why: The phrase is the most common use of the word. It functions almost as a single instruction: do not group by theme, do not rank by importance, follow the clock.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是该词最常见的用法。它几乎等于一条单一指令：不要按主题分组，不要按重要性排序，跟着钟表走。

intro.en: Chronological is chronology plus -ical. Chronology was rebuilt in Renaissance Latin from two Greek elements: khronos, 'time', and -logia, 'account or study'. The compound is not classical Greek but a scholarly construction, and chronological came to English through French. Its core meaning has stayed remarkably stable: put events on one line and read them in order.
intro.cn: chronological 是 chronology 加 -ical。chronology 是文艺复兴拉丁语用两个希腊成分重建的：khronos“时间”与 -logia“论述、学问”。这个复合词不是古典希腊语，而是学术构造；chronological 经法语进入英语。其核心义一直相当稳定：把事件放在一条线上，按顺序读。

items.en: Khronos meant 'time' as a span or a period. Its deeper origin is uncertain; linguists have proposed connections with words for cutting or separating, but none is securely established.
items.cn: khronos 指作为一段跨度或时期的时间。它的更深来源不确定；语言学家提出过与“切割、分离”类词的关联，但没有一种被可靠确立。

items.en: Logia, from logos, meant 'speaking, account, reasoned study'. In compounds it named a field of inquiry, as in biology or theology.
items.cn: logia 来自 logos，意为“言说、记述、有理据的探讨”。在复合词中它命名一个研究领域，如 biology 或 theology。

items.en: The compound chronologia was formed by early modern scholars, not attested in classical Greek. It named the study of dates and the arrangement of events in time.
items.cn: 复合词 chronologia 由近代早期学者构造，不见于古典希腊语。它命名对日期的研究以及把事件按时间排列的工作。

items.en: French added -ique to form the adjective chronologique. English borrowed it as chronological in the 16th to 17th century, a date best given as approximate.
items.cn: 法语加 -ique 构成形容词 chronologique。英语在 16 至 17 世纪借入为 chronological，这个年代只能大致给出。

items.en: In English the adjective was used for both the discipline and the arrangement. Historians applied it to annals; scientists later applied it to strata and to measured sequences.
items.cn: 在英语中，这个形容词既用于学科，也用于排列。历史学家用它指编年史；科学家后来用它指地层与可量度的序列。

items.en: Modern usage extends to timelines, data logs, age measures and reverse-ordered feeds. The suffix -ical merely marks the adjectival form; the meaning still comes from the two Greek parts.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到时间轴、数据日志、年龄度量与倒序信息流。后缀 -ical 只标示形容词形式；意义仍来自两个希腊部分。

note.en: The first group separates chronological from two relatives from the same root and from one close adverb. The second group compares words that also deal with order in time.
note.cn: 第一组把 chronological 与两个同根亲属及一个形近副词分开。第二组比较同样处理时间顺序的词。

entries.definition: lasting a long time, said of illness or problems. It shares the Greek root for time but means 'long-drawn-out', not 'in time order'.
entries.definitionCN: 持续很久的，用于疾病或问题。它与“时间”共享希腊词根，但意为“长期的”，不是“按时间排列”。

entries.definition: the study of dates, or an ordered list of events. Chronological is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 年代学，或按顺序排列的事件表。chronological 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: in time order. The adverb modifies a verb; the adjective modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间顺序地。副词修饰动词；形容词修饰名词。

entries.definition: following in a series. It stresses succession and can apply to steps that have no time element at all.
entries.definitionCN: 依次相随的。它强调接续，也可用于完全没有时间要素的步骤。

entries.definition: relating to time in general, as opposed to space or eternity. It does not by itself imply an order.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间本身有关，相对于空间或永恒。它本身并不含“有序”。

entries.definition: coming one after the other without interruption. It can describe generations or attempts, not only dates.
entries.definitionCN: 接连不断相随的。它可描述世代或尝试，不只描述日期。

entries.definition: relating to past events as studied by history. A historical account may be thematic, while a chronological one must follow dates.
entries.definitionCN: 与历史研究的过去事件有关。历史叙述可以按主题，而编年叙述必须跟着日期。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Greek halves of the word and then tie it to the everyday places where the order matters.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用词的两个希腊半部，再把它系到日常需要讲究次序的地方。

normal.en: Split it: chrono (time) plus logical (ordered). Time plus order is the whole word.
normal.cn: 拆开：chrono（时间）加 logical（有逻辑的）。时间加秩序就是整个词。

normal.en: Picture beads on a string, each bead one event.
normal.cn: 想象一串珠子，每颗珠子是一个事件。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: chronological order versus reverse chronological order.
normal.cn: 对比这一对：正序时间与倒序时间。

normal.en: Keep the psychology pair: chronological age against biological age.
normal.cn: 记住心理学那一对：实际年龄与生理年龄。

normal.en: Watch the trap word chronic: same root, completely different meaning.
normal.cn: 提防陷阱词 chronic：同根，意义完全不同。

abstract.en: Hold one axis: a single line from left to right. Every sense either puts something on that line or studies the line itself.
abstract.cn: 抓住一条轴：从左到右的一条线。每个义项要么把某物放上这条线，要么研究这条线本身。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by what is ordered: events, dates, records, people, stories, rocks, charts, ages, and the fixed phrase.
abstract.cn: 按被排序的对象分组：事件、日期、记录、人、故事、岩石、图表、年龄，以及固定短语。

abstract.en: Notice what the word refuses to do: it does not rank importance or explain causes, it only says what came first.
abstract.cn: 留意这个词拒绝做的事：它不排重要性，也不解释原因，只说明什么先发生。

examples.en: Read the chapters in chronological order to follow the argument.
examples.cn: 按章节的时间顺序阅读，以跟上论证。

examples.en: Her chronological age is forty, though she looks younger.
examples.cn: 她的实际年龄是四十岁，虽然看起来更年轻。

examples.en: The archive is organised in reverse chronological order.
examples.cn: 该档案馆按倒序时间排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“克若诺逻辑可”：chrono 是时间，logical 是讲逻辑——按时间的逻辑排下去，就是 chronological，按时间顺序的。

root: 希腊语 khronos“时间”加 -logia“论述、学问”，文艺复兴拉丁语构造为 chronologia；法语加 -ique 成 chronologique，英语借入为 chronological（chronology + -ical）。

sensesIntro.en: Chronological is one of the most obedient adjectives in English: it follows the clock and nothing else. Its nine senses all place something on a single line — letters, negotiations, children, film scenes, rock layers, timelines, ages — or describe the discipline that builds that line. When a text is called chronological, the point is usually that it has refused to reorganise time for effect.
sensesIntro.cn: chronological 是英语中最守规矩的形容词之一：它只跟着钟表，别的都不管。它的九个义项都把某物放上同一条线——信件、谈判、孩子、电影场景、岩层、时间轴、年龄——或者描述建立这条线的学问。当一段文字被称为 chronological，重点通常是它拒绝为了效果而重排时间。

core.en: One axis only: what came first, what came next.
core.cn: 只有一条轴：什么先来，什么后到。

branches.en: ORDER: the plain arrangement and its fixed phrase.
branches.cn: 顺序：朴素的排列及其固定短语。

branches.en: RECORD: the discipline of dating and the sequence it produces.
branches.cn: 记录：断代的学问及其产生的序列。

branches.en: PEOPLE: age order, and actual age measured against other ages.
branches.cn: 人：年龄顺序，以及与他种年龄对照的实际年龄。

branches.en: STORY: narrative that refuses flashbacks.
branches.cn: 故事：拒绝倒叙的叙述。

branches.en: EARTH AND CHART: strata read upward, time drawn as length.
branches.cn: 大地与图表：自下而上读的地层，被画成长度的时间。

intro.en: Chronological carries two Greek pieces and one Latin suffix: khronos, -logia and -ical. The items below follow that build, then add the related forms that share the root for time, including two words that drifted far from 'order'.
intro.cn: chronological 带着两个希腊成分与一个拉丁后缀：khronos、-logia 与 -ical。下面的条目沿这个构造展开，再加上共享“时间”词根的关联形式，其中两个词已经远离“顺序”义。

latinIntro.en: The entries are Latinised Greek rather than native Latin: chronologia is a Renaissance coinage, chronicus is the Latin form of Greek khronikos, and chronographia names the writing of time. They are included as the Latin channel through which English received these forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这些条目是拉丁化的希腊词，而非本土拉丁语：chronologia 是文艺复兴造词，chronicus 是希腊 khronikos 的拉丁形式，chronographia 指对时间的记录。列入它们，是因为英语正是通过拉丁渠道接收这些形式。

senses.title: The spice

intro.en: Cinnamon comes through Greek kinnamomon and Latin from a Semitic name for the bark.

items.en: The name begins in a Semitic language.

items.en: Latin keeps the spice name.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留香料名。

items.en: English shortens it to cinnamon.

items.en: The spice trade spreads its use.

items.en: Cinnamon also names a colour.
items.cn: 现代也指一种颜色。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cinn- opening; the near-meaning group lists warm spices.

entries.definition: A spice of the parsley family.

normalIntro.en: A curled piece of bark that smells like warm kitchens.
normalIntro.cn: 一片卷起的树皮，闻起来像温暖的厨房。

normal.en: The name came through Greek.

A stick curls as it dries.

The colour borrows the name.

abstract.en: Warmth you can smell.
A bark that learned to bake.
Brown with a memory of fire.

definition_zh: prep./adv. 大约（用于年代或数量，尤见于学术与展签）

items.en: Circum means around.
items.cn: circum 意为环绕。

core_image: 粉笔在黑板上画出的一个闭合圆圈

senses.title: A round closed shape
senses.definition: a perfectly round shape whose edge is the same distance from the centre everywhere

senses.example: He drew a circle on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在黑板上画了一个圆。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who share an interest or a way of life

senses.example: She has a small circle of close friends.

senses.whyCN: 围着说话人站成一圈的人，逐渐成了一群社交伙伴。

senses.title: To move around something

intro.en: Circle comes from the Latin word for a small ring.
intro.cn: circle 源自拉丁语中表示小圆环的词。

items.en: Circus named a ring or a circular arena.
items.cn: circus 指圆环或环形场地。

items.en: Circulus was the small ring built from circus.
items.cn: circulus 是由 circus 构成的指小形式，意为小圆环。

items.en: Cercle carried the shape word into French.
items.cn: cercle 把这个表示形状的词带进法语。

items.en: English circle named the shape and the ring of people.
items.cn: 英语 circle 兼指形状与围成圈的人群。

items.en: The noun produced a verb meaning to go round.
items.cn: 这个名词又生出表示绕行的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the circus root, the ring of people and the verb of going round.

normal.en: Circle and circus share a root: a circus is played inside a big ring.
